sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tatas te sahitā vīrāḥ prayātā dakṣiṇāmukhāḥ upāstamayavelāyāṃ śibirābhyāśam āgatāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then those heroes, banded together, set out facing southward, and as the hour of sunset drew near they came to the neighborhood of the camp.

sanskrit: vimucya vāhāṃs tvaritā bhītāḥ samabhavaṃs tadā gahanaṃ deśam āsādya pracchannā nyaviśanta te
english: Hastily unyoking their mounts, they grew afraid; and reaching a dense thicket, they settled there, hidden from view.

sanskrit: senāniveśam abhito nātidūram avasthitāḥ nikṛttā niśitaiḥ śastraiḥ samantāt kṣatavikṣatāḥ
english: They halted not far off, near the army's encampment, hacked by sharp weapons and gashed with wounds on every side.

sanskrit: dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya pāṇḍavān anvacintayan śrutvā ca ninadaṃ ghoraṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ jayaiṣiṇām
english: Breathing long, hot sighs, they brooded upon the Pāṇḍavas, having heard the terrible uproar of the Pāṇḍavas hungry for victory.

sanskrit: anusārabhayād bhītāḥ prāṅmukhāḥ prādravan punaḥ te muhūrtaṃ tato gatvā śrāntavāhāḥ pipāsitāḥ
english: Afraid of pursuit, in terror they fled again, this time turned eastward; and after going on for a short while, their mounts spent and themselves athirst,

sanskrit: nāmṛṣyanta maheṣvāsāḥ krodhāmarṣavaśaṃ gatāḥ rājño vadhena saṃtaptā muhūrtaṃ samavasthitāḥ
english: those mighty archers could bear it no longer, falling under the sway of wrath and indignation; tormented by the slaying of their king, they halted for a moment.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca aśraddheyam idaṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhīmena saṃjaya yat sa nāgāyutaprāṇaḥ putro mama nipātitaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Unbelievable is this deed wrought by Bhīma, Saṃjaya—that my son, whose strength was that of ten thousand elephants, has been struck down.

sanskrit: avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vajrasaṃhanano yuvā pāṇḍavaiḥ samare putro nihato mama saṃjaya
english: Unslayable by all beings, his frame hard as the thunderbolt, my son in his youth has been killed in battle by the Pāṇḍavas, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: na diṣṭam abhyatikrāntuṃ śakyaṃ gāvalgaṇe naraiḥ yat sametya raṇe pārthaiḥ putro mama nipātitaḥ
english: It is not possible, O son of Gavalgaṇa, for men to overstep what fate decrees—since, having closed with the sons of Pṛthā in battle, my son has been brought down.

sanskrit: adrisāramayaṃ nūnaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama saṃjaya hataṃ putraśataṃ śrutvā yan na dīrṇaṃ sahasradhā
english: Surely my heart is made of the very substance of stone, Saṃjaya, for on hearing that a hundred sons are slain it has not burst into a thousand shards.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi vṛddhamithunaṃ hataputraṃ bhaviṣyati na hy ahaṃ pāṇḍaveyasya viṣaye vastum utsahe
english: How shall an aged couple endure the loss of their sons? For I have no heart to dwell within the realm of the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: kathaṃ rājñaḥ pitā bhūtvā svayaṃ rājā ca saṃjaya preṣyabhūtaḥ pravarteyaṃ pāṇḍaveyasya śāsanāt
english: How, having been father of a king and myself a king, Saṃjaya, am I to live on as a servant, at the command of the son of Pāṇḍu?

sanskrit: ājñāpya pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ sthitvā mūrdhni ca saṃjaya katham adya bhaviṣyāmi preṣyabhūto durantakṛt
english: Having commanded the whole earth and stood at its very summit, Saṃjaya, how shall I now become a servant, I who once wrought deeds past all bounds?

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhīmasya vākyāni śrotuṃ śakṣyāmi saṃjaya yena putraśataṃ pūrṇam ekena nihataṃ mama
english: How, Saṃjaya, shall I be able to hear the words of Bhīma, by whom alone my full hundred sons have been slain?

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ satyaṃ vacas tasya vidurasya mahātmanaḥ akurvatā vacas tena mama putreṇa saṃjaya
english: True has been made the word of that great-souled Vidura, for that son of mine, Saṃjaya, would not act upon his counsel.

sanskrit: adharmeṇa hate tāta putre duryodhane mama kṛtavarmā kṛpo drauṇiḥ kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: When my son Duryodhana had been slain by foul means, dear Saṃjaya, what then did Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, and the son of Droṇa do?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca gatvā tu tāvakā rājan nātidūram avasthitāḥ apaśyanta vanaṃ ghoraṃ nānādrumalatākulam
english: Saṃjaya said: Having gone on, O king, your men halted not far away, and beheld a terrible forest thick with manifold trees and creepers.

sanskrit: te muhūrtaṃ tu viśramya labdhatoyair hayottamaiḥ sūryāstamayavelāyām āseduḥ sumahad vanam
english: Resting a while, with their fine horses now watered, at the hour of the sun's setting they reached a vast forest—

sanskrit: nānāmṛgagaṇair juṣṭaṃ nānāpakṣisamākulam nānādrumalatācchannaṃ nānāvyālaniṣevitam
english: frequented by herds of varied beasts, alive with birds of every kind, mantled in diverse trees and creepers, haunted by manifold serpents,

sanskrit: nānātoyasamākīrṇaṃ taḍāgair upaśobhitam padminīśatasaṃchannaṃ nīlotpalasamāyutam
english: strewn with many waters and graced with ponds, covered over with a hundred lotus-beds and bright with blue lilies.

sanskrit: praviśya tad vanaṃ ghoraṃ vīkṣamāṇāḥ samantataḥ śākhāsahasrasaṃchannaṃ nyagrodhaṃ dadṛśus tataḥ
english: Entering that fearsome forest and gazing about on every side, they then beheld a banyan veiled in a thousand boughs.

sanskrit: upetya tu tadā rājan nyagrodhaṃ te mahārathāḥ dadṛśur dvipadāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ taṃ vai vanaspatim
english: Approaching that banyan, O king, those great chariot-warriors, foremost among men, looked upon that finest of forest-lords.

sanskrit: te 'vatīrya rathebhyas tu vipramucya ca vājinaḥ upaspṛśya yathānyāyaṃ saṃdhyām anvāsata prabho
english: Dismounting from their chariots and unharnessing their horses, they sipped water as the rite ordains, O lord, and sat in worship of the twilight.

sanskrit: tato 'staṃ parvataśreṣṭham anuprāpte divākare sarvasya jagato dhātrī śarvarī samapadyata
english: Then, when the day-maker had passed to the foremost of mountains in the west, night came on, the sustainer of the whole world.

sanskrit: grahanakṣatratārābhiḥ prakīrṇābhir alaṃkṛtam nabho 'ṃśukam ivābhāti prekṣaṇīyaṃ samantataḥ
english: Adorned with planets, lunar mansions, and stars scattered abroad, the sky shone like a fair garment, lovely to behold on every side.

sanskrit: īṣac cāpi pravalganti ye sattvā rātricāriṇaḥ divācarāś ca ye sattvās te nidrāvaśam āgatāḥ
english: The creatures that roam by night began faintly to stir abroad, while the creatures that move by day passed into the power of sleep.

sanskrit: rātriṃcarāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ ninādo 'bhūt sudāruṇaḥ kravyādāś ca pramuditā ghorā prāptā ca śarvarī
english: Dreadful grew the cry of the night-roaming creatures, the eaters of raw flesh rejoiced, and the terrible night had come.

sanskrit: tasmin rātrimukhe ghore duḥkhaśokasamanvitāḥ kṛtavarmā kṛpo drauṇir upopaviviśuḥ samam
english: In that fearful onset of night, filled with anguish and grief, Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, and the son of Droṇa sat down together side by side.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭāḥ śocanto nyagrodhasya samantataḥ tam evārtham atikrāntaṃ kurupāṇḍavayoḥ kṣayam
english: Seated there, grieving all about the banyan, they brooded on that very matter now past undoing—the ruin of Kurus and Pāṇḍavas alike.

sanskrit: nidrayā ca parītāṅgā niṣedur dharaṇītale śrameṇa sudṛḍhaṃ yuktā vikṣatā vividhaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Their limbs overcome by sleep, they sank to the surface of the earth, bound fast by weariness and torn with arrows of every kind.

sanskrit: tato nidrāvaśaṃ prāptau kṛpabhojau mahārathau sukhocitāv aduḥkhārhau niṣaṇṇau dharaṇītale tau tu suptau mahārāja śramaśokasamanvitau
english: Then the two great chariot-warriors, Kṛpa and the Bhoja, fell under the sway of sleep—men used to ease and undeserving of pain—and lay down upon the bare earth; and those two slept, O great king, worn out with toil and sorrow.

sanskrit: krodhāmarṣavaśaṃ prāpto droṇaputras tu bhārata naiva sma sa jagāmātha nidrāṃ sarpa iva śvasan
english: But the son of Droṇa, O Bhārata, fallen under the sway of wrath and indignation, could in no way win his way to sleep, hissing like a serpent.

sanskrit: na lebhe sa tu nidrāṃ vai dahyamāno 'timanyunā vīkṣāṃ cakre mahābāhus tad vanaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: Sleep he gained not at all, burning with measureless fury; and the mighty-armed one let his gaze wander over that forest, terrible to behold.

sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇo vanoddeśaṃ nānāsattvair niṣevitam apaśyata mahābāhur nyagrodhaṃ vāyasāyutam
english: Surveying that quarter of the wood, haunted by manifold creatures, the mighty-armed one beheld the banyan thronged with crows.

sanskrit: tatra kākasahasrāṇi tāṃ niśāṃ paryaṇāmayan sukhaṃ svapantaḥ kauravya pṛthak pṛthag apāśrayāḥ
english: There thousands of crows were passing that night, sleeping at ease, O scion of Kuru, each roosting apart in its own place.

sanskrit: supteṣu teṣu kākeṣu visrabdheṣu samantataḥ so 'paśyat sahasāyāntam ulūkaṃ ghoradarśanam
english: While those crows slept untroubled all about, he beheld of a sudden an owl come gliding in, dreadful to behold—

sanskrit: mahāsvanaṃ mahākāyaṃ haryakṣaṃ babhrupiṅgalam sudīrghaghoṇānakharaṃ suparṇam iva veginam
english: loud of voice and huge of body, tawny-eyed, of dun and ruddy hue, with a very long beak and talons, swift as a fine-winged eagle.

sanskrit: so 'tha śabdaṃ mṛduṃ kṛtvā līyamāna ivāṇḍajaḥ nyagrodhasya tataḥ śākhāṃ prārthayām āsa bhārata
english: That bird, uttering a soft cry, as if stealing in unseen, made then for a bough of the banyan, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃnipatya tu śākhāyāṃ nyagrodhasya vihaṃgamaḥ suptāñ jaghāna subahūn vāyasān vāyasāntakaḥ
english: Alighting upon that bough of the banyan, that bird, the bane of crows, slew the sleeping crows in great numbers.

sanskrit: keṣāṃ cid acchinat pakṣāñ śirāṃsi ca cakarta ha caraṇāṃś caiva keṣāṃ cid babhañja caraṇāyudhaḥ
english: From some it sheared the wings, and the heads of some it lopped away; and the feet of others it broke off—that creature whose weapons were its claws.

sanskrit: kṣaṇenāhan sa balavān ye 'sya dṛṣṭipathe sthitāḥ teṣāṃ śarīrāvayavaiḥ śarīraiś ca viśāṃ pate nyagrodhamaṇḍalaṃ sarvaṃ saṃchannaṃ sarvato 'bhavat
english: In an instant the strong bird slew all that stood within the path of its sight; and with their severed limbs and bodies, O lord of peoples, the whole compass of the banyan was strewn over on every side.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu hatvā tataḥ kākān kauśiko mudito 'bhavat pratikṛtya yathākāmaṃ śatrūṇāṃ śatrusūdanaḥ
english: Having slain those crows, the owl rejoiced, that slayer of foes, taking its vengeance upon its enemies according to its heart's desire.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā sopadhaṃ karma kauśikena kṛtaṃ niśi tadbhāvakṛtasaṃkalpo drauṇir eko vyacintayat
english: Beholding that stealthy deed wrought by the owl in the night, the son of Droṇa, his resolve shaped to that very mind, pondered alone:

sanskrit: upadeśaḥ kṛto 'nena pakṣiṇā mama saṃyuge śatrūṇāṃ kṣapaṇe yuktaḥ prāptakālaś ca me mataḥ
english: "A lesson has this bird taught me for my own warfare, fit for the destruction of foes; and I deem the moment for it has come.

sanskrit: nādya śakyā mayā hantuṃ pāṇḍavā jitakāśinaḥ balavantaḥ kṛtotsāhā labdhalakṣāḥ prahāriṇaḥ rājñaḥ sakāśe teṣāṃ ca pratijñāto vadho mayā
english: The Pāṇḍavas, flushed with the show of victory, cannot be slain by me this day—they are strong, full of zeal, sure of their aim, and fierce in the strike; yet I have sworn their slaughter in the presence of my king.

sanskrit: pataṃgāgnisamāṃ vṛttim āsthāyātmavināśinīm nyāyato yudhyamānasya prāṇatyāgo na saṃśayaḥ chadmanā tu bhavet siddhiḥ śatrūṇāṃ ca kṣayo mahān
english: To take up a course like the moth's rush into the fire, that ends in one's own undoing—for one who fights by fair rule, the loss of life is beyond doubt; but by stratagem success may come, and a great destruction of the foe.

sanskrit: tatra saṃśayitād arthād yo 'rtho niḥsaṃśayo bhavet taṃ janā bahu manyante ye 'rthaśāstraviśāradāḥ
english: In such a case, the course that proves certain, set against the course of doubtful issue—that men hold in high esteem, those who are versed in the science of statecraft.

sanskrit: yac cāpy atra bhaved vācyaṃ garhitaṃ lokaninditam kartavyaṃ tan manuṣyeṇa kṣatradharmeṇa vartatā
english: And whatever in this would be blameworthy, censured, and condemned by the world—that too must a man do who walks in the warrior's law.

sanskrit: ninditāni ca sarvāṇi kutsitāni pade pade sopadhāni kṛtāny eva pāṇḍavair akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: And all manner of blameworthy, contemptible, and crooked deeds have been done at every step by the Pāṇḍavas, men of unmastered souls.

sanskrit: asminn arthe purā gītau śrūyete dharmacintakaiḥ ślokau nyāyam avekṣadbhis tattvārthaṃ tattvadarśibhiḥ
english: On this matter two verses sung of old are heard, framed by ponderers of the law, who looked to right reason—seers of the truth of things, who grasped its inmost sense:

sanskrit: pariśrānte vidīrṇe ca bhuñjāne cāpi śatrubhiḥ prasthāne ca praveśe ca prahartavyaṃ ripor balam
english: "When the enemy's host is spent, when it is scattered, when it is taking food, at its setting out and at its entering in—then is the foe's force to be struck.

sanskrit: nidrārtam ardharātre ca tathā naṣṭapraṇāyakam bhinnayodhaṃ balaṃ yac ca dvidhā yuktaṃ ca yad bhavet
english: Spent with sleep at the dead of night, and likewise when its leaders are lost, when its warriors are broken, and when the force is split in two—"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ niścayaṃ cakre suptānāṃ yudhi māraṇe pāṇḍūnāṃ saha pāñcālair droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān
english: Thus did the valorous son of Droṇa form his resolve—to slay in the night, while they slept, the sons of Pāṇḍu together with the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: sa krūrāṃ matim āsthāya viniścitya muhur muhuḥ suptau prābodhayat tau tu mātulaṃ bhojam eva ca
english: Fixing his mind upon that cruel purpose, and resolving on it again and again, he roused those two as they slept—his maternal uncle and the Bhoja.

sanskrit: nottaraṃ pratipede ca tatra yuktaṃ hriyā vṛtaḥ sa muhūrtam iva dhyātvā bāṣpavihvalam abravīt
english: He could find there no fitting answer, held back by shame; and after musing as it were a moment, choked with tears, he spoke:

sanskrit: hato duryodhano rājā ekavīro mahābalaḥ yasyārthe vairam asmābhir āsaktaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: "Slain is King Duryodhana, the matchless hero of mighty strength, for whose sake this feud of ours with the Pāṇḍavas was joined.

sanskrit: ekākī bahubhiḥ kṣudrair āhave śuddhavikramaḥ pātito bhīmasenena ekādaśacamūpatiḥ
english: Alone, by many base men, that lord of eleven armies, whose valor was pure, was brought down in battle by Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: vṛkodareṇa kṣudreṇa sunṛśaṃsam idaṃ kṛtam mūrdhābhiṣiktasya śiraḥ pādena parimṛdnatā
english: By base Vṛkodara this most cruel thing was done—that he ground with his foot the head of a king consecrated with the royal anointing.

sanskrit: vinardanti sma pāñcālāḥ kṣveḍanti ca hasanti ca dhamanti śaṅkhāñ śataśo hṛṣṭā ghnanti ca dundubhīn
english: The Pāñcālas roared aloud, they shouted and they laughed; in their hundreds, exultant, they blew their conches and beat their kettledrums.

sanskrit: vāditraghoṣas tumulo vimiśraḥ śaṅkhanisvanaiḥ anilenerito ghoro diśaḥ pūrayatīva hi
english: The tumultuous din of their instruments, mingled with the blare of conches and borne upon the wind, dreadful, seems to fill all the quarters of the sky.

sanskrit: aśvānāṃ heṣamāṇānāṃ gajānāṃ caiva bṛṃhatām siṃhanādaś ca śūrāṇāṃ śrūyate sumahān ayam
english: Of horses neighing and of elephants trumpeting, and the lions' roar of warriors—this mighty clamor is heard.

sanskrit: diśaṃ prācīṃ samāśritya hṛṣṭānāṃ garjatāṃ bhṛśam rathanemisvanāś caiva śrūyante lomaharṣaṇāḥ
english: From the eastern quarter, where the exultant ones roar fiercely, the very clatter of chariot-rims is heard, making the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavair dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ yad idaṃ kadanaṃ kṛtam vayam eva trayaḥ śiṣṭās tasmin mahati vaiśase
english: This slaughter of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra has been wrought by the Pāṇḍavas; and we three alone are left in that great carnage.

sanskrit: ke cin nāgaśataprāṇāḥ ke cit sarvāstrakovidāḥ nihatāḥ pāṇḍaveyaiḥ sma manye kālasya paryayam
english: Some who had the strength of a hundred elephants, some skilled in every weapon, have been slain by the sons of Pāṇḍu—I deem it the turning of Time.

sanskrit: evam etena bhāvyaṃ hi nūnaṃ kāryeṇa tattvataḥ yathā hy asyedṛśī niṣṭhā kṛte kārye 'pi duṣkare
english: Surely this end was fated to be, in very truth, by the working of that deed—seeing that such was its issue, even when the hard task had been accomplished.

sanskrit: bhavatos tu yadi prajñā na mohād apacīyate vyāpanne 'smin mahaty arthe yan naḥ śreyas tad ucyatām
english: But if the wisdom of you both has not, through bewilderment, been diminished, now that this great cause is undone, let that which is our welfare be spoken."

sanskrit: kṛpa uvāca śrutaṃ te vacanaṃ sarvaṃ hetuyuktaṃ mayā vibho mamāpi tu vacaḥ kiṃ cic chṛṇuṣvādya mahābhuja
english: Kṛpa said: All your words, well grounded in reason, have I heard, O lord; yet hear now some word of mine also, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: ābaddhā mānuṣāḥ sarve nirbandhāḥ karmaṇor dvayoḥ daive puruṣakāre ca paraṃ tābhyāṃ na vidyate
english: All men are bound, held fast, by two kinds of working—by fate and by human effort; beyond these two there is nothing.

sanskrit: na hi daivena sidhyanti karmāṇy ekena sattama na cāpi karmaṇaikena dvābhyāṃ siddhis tu yogataḥ
english: For deeds are not brought to fulfillment by fate alone, O noblest one, nor yet by effort alone; success comes only from the joining of the two.

sanskrit: tābhyām ubhābhyāṃ sarvārthā nibaddhā hy adhamottamāḥ pravṛttāś caiva dṛśyante nivṛttāś caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: By these two together are all undertakings bound, the lowest and the highest alike; and they are seen both set in motion and held back in every way.

sanskrit: parjanyaḥ parvate varṣan kiṃ nu sādhayate phalam kṛṣṭe kṣetre tathāvarṣan kiṃ nu sādhayate phalam
english: The rain-cloud, pouring upon a mountain, what fruit does it bring to pass? And withholding its rain from a ploughed field, what fruit does it then bring to pass?

sanskrit: utthānaṃ cāpy adaivasya hy anutthānasya daivatam vyarthaṃ bhavati sarvatra pūrvaṃ kas tatra niścayaḥ
english: The exertion that lacks fate's favor, and fate that lacks exertion—each is everywhere in vain; which of them, then, comes first, who can decide?

sanskrit: pravṛṣṭe ca yathā deve samyak kṣetre ca karṣite bījaṃ mahāguṇaṃ bhūyāt tathā siddhir hi mānuṣī
english: As, when the god of rain has poured well and the field is rightly ploughed, the seed yields a rich abundance—even so is success that is wrought by man.

sanskrit: tayor daivaṃ viniścitya svavaśenaiva vartate prājñāḥ puruṣakāraṃ tu ghaṭante dākṣyam āsthitāḥ
english: Of these two, fate ordains its course wholly by its own will; but the wise, taking their stand on diligence, strive on through human effort.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ sarve hi kāryārthā manuṣyāṇāṃ nararṣabha viceṣṭantaś ca dṛśyante nivṛttāś ca tathaiva hi
english: For by these two are all the aims of men's undertakings governed, O bull among men; and they are seen both striving forward and likewise held back.

sanskrit: kṛtaḥ puruṣakāraḥ san so 'pi daivena sidhyati tathāsya karmaṇaḥ kartur abhinirvartate phalam
english: Even human effort, once made, comes to its fulfillment by fate; and so for the doer of that deed the fruit is brought to pass.

sanskrit: utthānaṃ tu manuṣyāṇāṃ dakṣāṇāṃ daivavarjitam aphalaṃ dṛśyate loke samyag apy upapāditam
english: But the exertion of able men, when fate is wanting, is seen in the world to bear no fruit, even though rightly carried through.

sanskrit: tatrālasā manuṣyāṇāṃ ye bhavanty amanasvinaḥ utthānaṃ te vigarhanti prājñānāṃ tan na rocate
english: Thereupon the slothful among men, those who are dull of spirit, decry exertion; but to the wise that thinking is not pleasing.

sanskrit: prāyaśo hi kṛtaṃ karma aphalaṃ dṛśyate bhuvi akṛtvā ca punar duḥkhaṃ karma dṛśyen mahāphalam
english: For most often a deed once done is seen to bear no fruit on earth; and again, a deed not done is, to one's sorrow, seen to have borne great fruit.

sanskrit: ceṣṭām akurvaṃl labhate yadi kiṃ cid yadṛcchayā yo vā na labhate kṛtvā durdaśau tāv ubhāv api
english: If one who makes no effort yet gains something by mere chance, or one who, having made his effort, gains nothing—both these are in sorry case alike.
